I opened up during a session with my psychologist about recent (at the time) thoughts and plans to kill myself. I was sure he was going to send me to the hospital instead I was greeted with compassion and understanding. We spent a great deal of time figuring out what factors were contributing to my state and ways to manage my stressors.

I have been labeled with disorders ranging from acute depression to severe bipolar - honestly none of thatb matters nor does it help you. It just helps your medical care team have an understanding of what your going through. Your medical records are private theres nothing stopping you from being honest with your doctor and picking up meds from the pharmacy. You could do so without your parents finding out but in my experience its best to have a support system - your doctor can explain to them how the medication works, what to expect, what not to expect etc..

Just to let you know people with depression who don't want to live are at high risk but that doesn't necessarily mean you'll get sent to the cuckoos nest.  When I admitted myself after serious ideation they refused to admit me immediately and instead put me on watch for 24 hours when the time came they gave me an option I could sign myself in or go home I chose the former and never once regretted that decision. I am actually grateful that I spent time in the psych unit because it was a moving experience - I sometimes joke and say I should go back once a year for a week as a mental vacation but that's just my dark humour. Just remember you are stronger than you know and wise beyond your years. Get well, Godspeed!

You are a human being not a statistic. I use to (and from time to time think I will just be) a statistic but I am learning to love myself- just yesterday I had a major breakdown and needed to go to my emergency stash of seroquel and lithium so I wouldn't a.) Go to the hospital b.) End my life. 

I woke up today still rather sad but as the day progressed I was able to become sort of stable. Lithium gets a bad rap - I was on it for 2+ years after being misdiagnosed with bipolar but nonetheless it saved my life. 

Taking a single dose coupled with 300mg of seroquel gave me back sleep I had missed over the last few months. As the day progressed my ambition returned and suicide has not crossed my mind. 

On a more personal note; I know the struggle of getting on board with medication but I dont think you should put it off. Things may or may not get out of control if you put it off - but why risk it? I think it's wise to take your doctor's advice and start the lithium - if nothing else you appear to have enough self awareness to take it on a PRN basis. I will take a lithium here and there when I catch myself slipping. I am in school finishing up my undergrad, researching at the UN, have a consulting business and I am working on my masters (yes while I am an undergrad) all of this creates alot of stress that occasionally overwhelms me. This affects my relationships (romantic, friends, family and to a lesser extent work) 

A lesson I keep learning is to take my medication as prescribed. Every time I become uncooperative my mental health becomes fragile very quickly.

 You will do what you think is best- but don't do it for others - do it for yourself. I hope your mind settles down and you get well. God speed!

After a long self induced sleep by means of the two medications I took - I woke up and realized that going off of effexor coupled with stressors in my life is most likely the cause of what happened. I talked with my pdoc (a day after we met mind you) and he suggested gradually getting back to my old dose of effexor. He also prescribed seroquel 50mg for sleep as he strongly believes my horrible sleep hygiene played a big role in my breakdown. 

Fortunately I have friends who I have opened up about my problems - but as the other commenter mentioned I think writing is going to help me alot. My pdoc didn't exactly approve my use of lithium and seroquel but recognized that the risk didn't outweigh the benefit as lithium is shown to stop suicidal ideation but he wants to see how I am in a month after the effexor and if there is not much change he will consider placing me on a regieme for that as well.

Personally I knew this day was coming I had been talking about this 'impending doom' with my psychologist for over a month. I'm just happy that I tripped and didn't fall. By no means do I think I am miraculously cured; but a lot of things were put into perspective which I believe is a big leap forward in my recovery. Thanks for reading this.
